memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Epilepsy diagnosed based on two witnessed tonic-clonic seizures and normal neurological exam.
Symptoms: episodic loss of consciousness with limb jerking, no post‑ictal confusion. Examination: alert, oriented, cranial nerves normal, motor strength 5/5 bilaterally, no focal deficits.
Smoking status: never.
Inhaler technique: not applicable (no inhaler prescribed).
Spirometry: FEV1 2.85 L (92% predicted), FVC 3.40 L, FEV1/FVC 0.84; change since prior test N/A.
Asthma Control Test score: 22 (well controlled).
Plan: start levetiracetam 500 mg BD and lamotrigine 50 mg BD; arrange EEG; check serum sodium and creatinine; review in 8 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Levetiracetam 500 mg oral tablet twice daily
Lamotrigine 50 mg oral tablet twice daily

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum Sodium: 138 mmol/L (135-145)
Serum Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (0.6-1.1)

memories.author: D05
memories.text: EEG (awake and sleep): background normal rhythm; occasional left temporal sharp waves noted, no epileptiform discharges during hyperventilation or photic stimulation. Suggestive of mild cortical irritability, consistent with epilepsy.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Epilepsy stable on current regimen; no seizures reported since medication start.
Symptoms: occasional mild headache, no aura. Examination: vitals normal, neuro exam unchanged.
Smoking status: never.
Inhaler technique: Technique checked: correct (using salbutamol metered-dose inhaler for occasional wheeze).
Spirometry: FEV1 2.90 L (94% predicted), FVC 3.42 L, FEV1/FVC 0.85; change in FEV1 since last test +0.05 L.
Asthma Control Test score: 22 (well controlled).
Plan: continue levetiracetam 500 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD; repeat labs in 3 months; review in 2 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Levetiracetam 750 mg oral tablet twice daily
Lamotrigine 50 mg oral tablet twice daily

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve felt a bit light‑headed and nauseous since increasing the levetiracetam dose two weeks ago. The seizures haven’t returned, but I’m worried about the side effects.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Possible levetiracetam‑related dizziness noted; seizure freedom maintained.
Symptoms: mild dizziness in mornings, no nausea on exam. Examination: alert, gait steady, no nystagmus.
Smoking status: never.
Inhaler technique: Technique checked: correct (salbutamol MDI).
Spirometry: FEV1 2.88 L (93% predicted), FVC 3.38 L, FEV1/FVC 0.85; change in FEV1 since last test –0.02 L.
Asthma Control Test score: 20 (well controlled).
Plan: reduce levetiracetam to 600 mg BD; monitor symptoms; check serum sodium and creatinine in 4 weeks; review in 6 weeks.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum Sodium: 136 mmol/L (135-145)
Serum Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL (0.6-1.1)

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Referral to Neurology for optimisation of epilepsy management and consideration of possible medication taper.
Reason: patient on stable regimen with occasional drug‑related side effects; seeking specialist input on long‑term control.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Neurology review: patient seizure‑free on levetiracetam 600 mg BD and lamotrigine 50 mg BD. Recommend maintaining current doses, monitor levetiracetam level if available, consider gradual lamotrigine taper after 6 months seizure‑free. Return to pulmonology for routine follow‑up.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up pulmonology appointment booked for 2026-03-15 at 10:30 AM with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Epilepsy well controlled; no seizures in past year; mild dizziness resolved after dose adjustment.
Symptoms: none. Examination: normal vitals, neuro exam intact.
Smoking status: never.
Inhaler technique: Technique checked: correct (salbutamol MDI).
Spirometry: FEV1 2.92 L (95% predicted), FVC 3.45 L, FEV1/FVC 0.85; change in FEV1 since last test +0.04 L.
Asthma Control Test score: 23 (well controlled).
Plan: continue levetiracetam 600 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD; annual labs; review in 6 months.
